summary: 30-year-old woman at 24 weeks who stopped her inhaled steroid for fear of harming the baby: 3 days of wheeze, PEF 60 % of predicted, speaking in sentences, SpO₂ 96 %. BTS/SIGN: treat as non-pregnant, do not withhold steroids.

inputs.hpi: 24 weeks pregnant. Stopped her preventer inhaler at 10 weeks, worried about the baby. Three days of wheeze and night-time cough, using salbutamol 4-6 times a day. Referred for perianal pain (thrombosed haemorrhoid, settling).

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Moderate asthma exacerbation in pregnancy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Moderate asthma exacerbation at 24 weeks (PEF 60%): salbutamol, prednisolone course, restart inhaled steroid - treat as for a non-pregnant woman; obstetric team informed.

mustInclude.note: Oral and inhaled steroids should not be withheld in pregnancy.

guideline.name: BTS/SIGN 158 - British guideline on the management of asthma
guideline.section: Section 9 acute asthma in adults: acute severe = PEF 33-50% best/predicted, RR >=25/min, HR >=110/min or inability to complete sentences; life-threatening = PEF <33%, SpO2 <92%, silent chest, cyanosis, poor respiratory effort, arrhythmia, exhaustion, altered consciousness, hypotension; oxygen to SpO2 94-98%, high-dose inhaled beta2 agonist, ipratropium in severe/life-threatening, prednisolone 40-50 mg, IV magnesium sulphate for severe asthma not responding; Section 12 pregnancy: treat as in non-pregnant patients, do not withhold steroids, fetal monitoring in acute severe asthma
guideline.citation: British Thoracic Society / Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. SIGN 158. Edinburgh: SIGN; 2019.

rationale: Pregnancy permutation: undertreatment (stopping inhaled steroids) is the commonest harm; guidelines say treat as non-pregnant.
